_comment: Curated headline summaries per event. NOT real news clippings — these are short factual summaries written for narrative context in the briefing's 'historical context' section. Used by search_news_archive. Source attribution is the public reference URL from each event row in seed/events.sql.

items.headline: Lehman Brothers files Chapter 11 — largest US bankruptcy at $613B in liabilities.
Reserve Primary Fund 'breaks the buck' as money-market panic spreads.
AIG receives $85B Fed loan facility to avert insolvency.
Fed, ECB, BoE, BoC, Sweden's Riksbank, and SNB cut policy rates by 50bps in coordinated action.
Fed funds target lowered to 1.5%; statement cites 'weakening of economic activity'.
Dow Jones falls ~1000 points in minutes before recovering most of the loss; SEC and CFTC launch investigation.
Trading firms point to algorithmic feedback loops in S&P e-mini futures as proximate trigger.
EU finance ministers approve €750B European Stabilization Mechanism in emergency session.
ECB announces sovereign bond purchase program; Greek 10Y yields fall sharply at the open.
Standard & Poor's lowers US sovereign credit rating to AA+, citing political brinkmanship.
S&P 500 falls 6.7% on first trading day after downgrade; Treasuries paradoxically rally.
FOMC adopts explicit calendar guidance: rates expected to remain near zero 'at least through mid-2013'.
Bernanke testimony to JEC suggests asset purchases could be tapered 'in the next few meetings'.
10Y Treasury yields rise 100bps over 6 weeks; emerging market currencies sell off broadly.
OPEC ministers in Vienna decline to cut production; Saudi Arabia signals strategy of defending market share.
Brent crude breaks below $60 — first time since 2009 — as US shale supply continues to grow.
PBoC resets daily yuan fixing mechanism; CNY drops 1.9% in largest one-day move in 20 years.
Global equity selloff intensifies — 'Black Monday' — Dow opens down 1000 points.
WTI crude trades below $27 — lowest level since May 2003 — amid global growth concerns.
UK votes 51.9%-48.1% to leave the European Union in surprise referendum result.
Sterling falls to 31-year low against dollar; FTSE 100 banks down 20%+.
Donald Trump wins US presidential election in surprise outcome over Hillary Clinton.
Overnight risk-off reverses sharply; banks, defense, and infrastructure lead a 1.1% S&P rally.
S&P 500 falls 4.1% as XIV (inverse VIX ETN) collapses 90% after-hours, triggering structural unwind.
Trump signs presidential memorandum imposing tariffs on $50B+ of Chinese imports.
China retaliates with proposed tariffs on $50B of US goods including soybeans, aircraft, and autos.
FOMC raises target range 25bps to 2.25-2.50%; dot plot shows two more 2019 hikes despite weakening data.
S&P 500 falls into bear-market territory on Christmas Eve; worst December for US stocks since 1931.
Trump tweets 10% tariffs on remaining $300B of Chinese imports starting September 1.
China lets yuan break 7.0 vs USD; Treasury formally labels China a currency manipulator.
S&P 500 falls 3.4% as Italian COVID-19 outbreak escalates; Lombardy and Veneto lock down.
WTI crude falls 25% on Saudi-Russia price war; S&P down 7.6% triggering circuit breaker.
Fed cuts target range to 0-0.25% on Sunday evening; restarts QE with $700B in planned purchases.
S&P 500 falls 12% — third-worst day in history — despite emergency Fed action.
Fed announces open-ended QE plus Primary and Secondary Market Corporate Credit Facilities.
S&P 500 rallies 9.4% — largest single-day gain since 1933 — confirming COVID equity bottom.
GME closes at $347, up from ~$20 three weeks prior; multiple hedge funds report large losses.
Robinhood restricts trading in GME, AMC, and other heavily shorted names; Congressional hearings follow.
WHO names new SARS-CoV-2 variant 'Omicron'; classified as a variant of concern.
S&P 500 falls 2.3% on a half-day Black Friday session; oil down 13% on demand fears.
Russian forces launch full-scale invasion of Ukraine across multiple fronts.
Brent crude breaches $100 for first time since 2014; European banks down ~10%.
WTI peaks above $130 amid US/UK Russian oil import bans.
FOMC raises target range 25bps to 0.25-0.50% — first increase of the cycle.
UK Chancellor Kwarteng announces £45B unfunded tax cuts; gilts and sterling fall sharply.
Bank of England announces emergency long-dated gilt purchases to halt LDI-driven feedback loop.
FDIC takes control of Silicon Valley Bank; second-largest US bank failure ever.
Fed announces Bank Term Funding Program; Treasury and FDIC guarantee all SVB and Signature Bank deposits.
UBS agrees to acquire Credit Suisse for CHF 3B in Swiss-government-orchestrated weekend deal.
~$17B in Credit Suisse AT1 bonds wiped out, junior to equity — shocking AT1 credit markets globally.
Fitch lowers US sovereign credit rating to AA+, citing fiscal trajectory and governance.
Hamas conducts large-scale attack from Gaza into Israel; Israel declares state of war.
Brent crude opens up 4% on Middle East war risk premium.
Nikkei 225 closes down 12.4% — worst day since 1987 Black Monday — as yen carry trade unwinds.
VIX spikes intraday to 65, third-highest reading on record after 2008 and 2020.
NVDA falls 17% — largest single-day market cap loss in history at ~$590B — on AI capex repricing concerns.
DeepSeek's R1 release reportedly trained on $5-6M GPU compute, prompting commoditization debate.
